title: On the Spectral Effects of Time Interval Subdivisions
content: This paper explores the irreducible nature of temporal intervals and their implications for quantum wavefunction propagation, drawing on the formal parallels between scalar diffraction theory and quantum mechanics. By treating temporal intervals as unified entities encoded in the frequency domain, this approach emphasizes the role of Fourier transforms in defining discrete, indivisible intervals. Attempts to subdivide such intervals introduce spectral artifacts, analogous to Gibbs ringing in signal processing, fundamentally altering the system’s physical characteristics. This framework challenges the notion of continuous time evolution and instead posits a holistic view where discrete intervals define the trajectory of quantum systems. Experimental implications are discussed, including applications in time-energy entanglement, attosecond light pulses, analyzing starlight, and quantum cryptography. Ontological implications are discussed.
